thread.title: Apple Sits Out As Microsoft, IBM Boost Dow; Bitcoin Trims Loss

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple Sits Out As Microsoft, IBM Boost Dow; Bitcoin Trims Loss
text:
Stocks extended their gains Wednesday as Boeing ( BA ), IBM ( IBM ) Intel ( INTC ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) boosted the Dow; Bitcoin pared its losses.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) led with a 0.9% gain, PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) advanced 0.8% and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) added 0.7%. Emerging markets outperformed with iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) up 1.4% to its best level since May 2011.
Sector funds scoring the biggest gains in the stock market today included semiconductors, metals miners and homebuilders. Gold miners, banks and telecom lagged.
VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) and iShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ) leapt more than 2% each. Chip gear maker ASML Holdings ( ASML ) gapped up and surged 6% to a new high after reporting solid Q4 results. It's now extended from a 186.47 cup-base buy point it cleared on Tuesday. The relative strength line is near a high.
Goldman Sachs ( GS ) fell nearly 3% to test support at its 50-day moving average. The big bank topped analyst forecasts but its trading operations underperformed rivals'. It was one of the Dow's biggest losers. But big-cap techs Intel, IBM and Microsoft rose more than 2% each to boost the blue chip index. Apple ( AAPL ) was fractionally lower. It's back near a 176.34 buy point of a flat base. While the iPhone maker is trading near record highs, its relative strength line has been lagging.
SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) and iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ) were slightly lower. Gold futures edged lower to $1,335.10 an ounce.
Bitcoin pared its loss to 12%, to $9,879.32, according to CoinDesk , after rising above $11,750 earlier. It fell to its lowest price since December. Other cryptocurrencies including Ethereum, Ripple and Litecoin also tumbled. BitConnect said late Tuesday it will close its exchange platform and lending services.
Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ) trimmed its deficit to 11%, though it's still below its 50-day line. Earlier, it gapped down and sank 14%. It's now 56% off its high and at its lowest level since Dec. 5. South Korea and China are among countries reportedly weighing a ban on cryptocurrencies.
Gold Rush? While Bitcoin has been hogging the spotlight, gold has been making a run, with two gold exchange traded funds staging recent breakouts.
"Since the Fed lifted rates last month, gold has behaved just as it did following the last two December rate hikes — that is, it's begun to appreciate," U.S. Global Investors CEO Frank Holmes said in a recent blog post. "On the final trading day of 2017, gold broke above $1,300 an ounce, a psychologically important level, and has since climbed an additional 1%. This is the first year since 2013, in fact, that gold has started the year above $1,300."
SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ), up 8% the past month, remains in buy range after clearing a 125.95 cup-with-handle buy point Friday. Shares are at their highest level in four months. They also offered an earlier entry at 124.07, from a double-bottom base. GLD advanced 4% from a late-August flat-base breakout to a Sept. 7 intraday high.
The $35.4 billion fund, which turned 13 in November, tracks the price of gold bullion. Its one-year return of 11.5% through Jan. 12, according   lags the S&P 500's 25.2% gain. GLD's 10-year average annual return of 3.7% also trails the 9.4% gain of the S&P 500 over the same time frame.
IShares Gold Trust ( IAU ), which also tracks gold futures, is just above a 12.84 buy point of a lopsided cup with handle. It's traced a similar pattern to GLD. IAU climbed more than 3% from its late-August breakout to its Sept. 7 peak.
The fund, which will mark its 13th anniversary next week, has gathered $10.6 billion in assets. Its one-year and 10-year returns were 11.7% and 3.8%, respectively. Both GLD and IAU saw an average annual loss over the past five years.
IAU carries a 0.25% expense ratio; GLD sports a 0.40% expense ratio. Both funds were featured in this ETF column on Dec. 29.
A nonphysical asset, Bitcoin, has recently stolen gold's thunder, both on the way up and the way down. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ), which aims to track the price of the underlying digital currency, soared more than 2,700% last year through mid-December. It's now down 50% from its peak.
